title: The Balance Sheet Equation
context: Analyze how the balance sheet equation requires total assets to equal the sum of total liabilities and total equity. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: A pallet loader used by an operating business is classified as inventory because inventory can include any physical equipment a business owns.
A pallet loader held by a dealer for resale to customers is classified as a non-current asset because the dealer is a business rather than a household.
A pallet loader kept in service by an operating business for more than one year is classified as a non-current tangible asset.
The same pallet loader must always be classified identically on every balance sheet regardless of how it is held.
The same pallet loader may be a non-current asset for one business and inventory for another, depending on whether it is used or held for sale.
tactical_explanations:
Physical form alone does not make a pallet loader inventory. Inventory is held for sale or for cycle consumption — not every machine the firm owns.

Operating use beyond a year puts pallet loader among non-current tangibles.

So the statement is False.

A dealer’s pallet loader held for customers is merchandise. Resale intent keeps it in inventory (current), even though the dealer is a firm.

Being a business does not override the held-for-sale test.

So the statement is False.

Multi-year operating use of a pallet loader fits the non-current tangible test.

Useful life beyond the period plus own use — not resale — drive that line.

So the statement is True.

The same pallet loader need not share one balance-sheet line everywhere. Each reporter classifies by how it holds the object.

Operator → non-current tangible; dealer → inventory.

Note: The same physical item can be inventory for a dealer and a fixed asset for an operator.

So the statement is False.

Intended use decides the line for the same physical object.

An operator records a non-current tangible; a dealer records inventory.

So the statement is True.

title: Assets Equal Liabilities Plus Equity
context: Review how owner's equity is derived as the residual claim remaining once liabilities are deducted from assets. Evaluate the following economic assertions:
statements: Classifying a pallet loader as a non-current asset depends mainly on its purchase price rather than on management's intended use.
Classifying a pallet loader as a non-current asset depends on management's intention to use it in operations rather than to sell it quickly.
A pallet loader acquired for resale still counts among non-current assets as long as it remains unsold for several months.
A pallet loader used daily in a business's own operations should be recorded as inventory because it wears out over time.
Once a dealer sells a pallet loader from its stock, the buyer must continue to record it as inventory.
tactical_explanations:
Purchase price measures cost; it does not choose inventory vs fixed asset. Management intent — operate or resell — decides the class.

A cheap pallet loader used for years is still non-current; a costly one held for sale is inventory.

So the statement is False.

Intent to use the asset in operations beyond one period places it among non-current assets.

Resale intent would have put the same object in inventory.

So the statement is True.

Goods bought for resale enter inventory immediately. Sitting unsold for months does not promote them into non-current assets.

Resale intent, not shelf time, decides the line.

So the statement is False.

Wear is handled by depreciating a fixed asset, not by calling operating kit inventory. Daily own use of a pallet loader supports non-current classification.

Counterexample: factory machines wear out yet sit in plant & equipment.

So the statement is False.

After the sale, the buyer’s purpose governs classification. If the buyer puts the machine into operations, it becomes the buyer’s non-current asset.

The seller’s old inventory label does not travel with the object forever.

So the statement is False.

title: Owner's Equity as a Residual Claim

A pallet loader bought by a business to support its own daily operations is a tangible fixed asset because it delivers benefit across several accounting periods.
A pallet loader that a dealer displays for sale is not a fixed asset of that dealer.
An industrial dishwasher kept in service by an operating business for more than one year is classified as a non-current tangible asset.
An industrial dishwasher held by a dealer for resale to customers is classified as inventory, a current asset, rather than a non-current asset.
tactical_explanations:
Bought to resell, a pallet loader belongs in inventory (current).

It is not an operating fixed asset of the buyer-dealer.

So the statement is True.

A pallet loader bought for the firm’s own daily work is a tangible fixed asset.

Benefit spans periods; it is not held for sale.

So the statement is True.

A dealer displaying a pallet loader for sale holds inventory.

That stock is not the dealer’s fixed asset.

So the statement is True.

Multi-year operating use of an industrial dishwasher fits the non-current tangible test.

Useful life beyond the period plus own use — not resale — drive that line.

So the statement is True.

Inventory is held for sale or cycle use and is classified as a current asset.

So the statement is True.
